questions.stem: Which blood component does carbon monoxide bind to?

options.explanation: Correct — this follows directly from the definition.
Carbon monoxide targets the oxygen carrier, not immune cells.
Platelets clot blood; they do not carry oxygen.
Plasma carries dissolved food, but carbon monoxide ignores it.

questions.stem: Why does carbon monoxide poisoning suffocate the body?

options.explanation: Swelling is not how carbon monoxide acts.

options.text: Because haemoglobin bound to carbon monoxide cannot carry oxygen
options.explanation: Yes — the mechanism works exactly this way.

options.text: Because the lungs fill with fluid
options.explanation: Fluid in the lungs is not the mechanism.
Cells do not burst; their oxygen seats are simply occupied.

questions.stem: How does sulfur dioxide produce acid rain?

options.text: It freezes into acid snow at ground level
options.explanation: The combination happens with water vapour in the air.
Cave chemistry is not the acid rain route.

options.text: It combines with water vapour in the atmosphere to form acidic rain
options.explanation: Correct — this matches the account taught above.

options.text: It burns forests directly with heat
options.explanation: The gas acts through rain chemistry, not direct heat.

questions.stem: Which system of the human body suffers from sulfur dioxide exposure?

options.explanation: Bones are not the target of sulfur dioxide.

options.text: The digestive system, ulcerating the gut
options.explanation: The gut is not the documented target here.
Respiration is the affected system.

options.text: The respiratory system, causing breathing problems
options.explanation: Right — this is the account the lesson teaches.

questions.stem: A lake loses its fish after acidic rain falls on its catchment. Which pollutant caused it?

options.text: Sulfur dioxide, through the acid rain it formed
options.explanation: Right — the other options each misplace a concept.
Carbon monoxide poisons blood, not lake water chemistry.
Methane drives warming, not lake acidification.
Nitrogen gas is inert and harmless here.

questions.stem: State the biological effect of carbon monoxide on oxygen transport.
questions.modelAnswer: Carbon monoxide binds to haemoglobin, reducing the transport of oxygen in the blood.

questions.stem: Name the kind of rain produced when sulfur dioxide combines with water vapour.
questions.modelAnswer: Sulfur dioxide combines with water vapour to form acid rain.

questions.stem: Explain why high carbon monoxide concentrations can be fatal.
questions.modelAnswer: High concentrations can be fatal because most haemoglobin becomes blocked, so the blood cannot deliver enough oxygen and the body suffocates.

questions.stem: A city reports both traffic smog and coal-burning haze. Match each hazard.
questions.modelAnswer: Traffic smog brings carbon monoxide, which blocks haemoglobin, while coal haze brings sulfur dioxide, which forms acid rain and irritates breathing.
